hints: Remember that for gases at the same conditions, volume ratio is the same as mole ratio, so use the balanced equation directly with cm3.
10 cm3 of CH3SH needs 3 x 10 = 30 cm3 of O2, so oxygen is in excess and 30 cm3 will be left over.
Check the physical state of each product at room temperature to decide which ones actually count toward the final gas volume.
walkthrough:
**Find the limiting reagent using gas volumes**

For gases, volume is proportional to moles, so we can use cm3 just like moles.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{SH} + 3\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{SO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Calculate oxygen used and left over**

1 volume of $\text{CH}_3\text{SH}$ needs 3 volumes of $\text{O}_2$.

$$\text{O}_2 \text{ needed} = 10 \times 3 = 30 \text{ cm}^3$$
You started with 60 cm3, so excess left is 60 - 30 = 30 cm3. All the 10 cm3 of $\text{CH}_3\text{SH}$ is used up.

**Find volumes of gaseous products**

From the equation, 1 volume of $\text{CH}_3\text{SH}$ makes 1 volume of $\text{CO}_2$ and 1 volume of $\text{SO}_2$.

$$\text{CO}_2 \text{ made} = 10 \text{ cm}^3, \quad \text{SO}_2 \text{ made} = 10 \text{ cm}^3$$
This is the key trick. Water, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, is a liquid at room temperature, so its 20 cm3 does NOT count as gas.

**Add up the gases that remain**

Final gas mixture = leftover $\text{O}_2$ + $\text{CO}_2$ + $\text{SO}_2$.

$$V_{final} = 30 + 10 + 10 = 50 \text{ cm}^3$$

options.A: 20 cm3 is just the two gaseous products, 10 cm3 CO2 + 10 cm3 SO2. It correctly leaves out liquid water but forgets to add the 30 cm3 of excess oxygen that is still present as a gas.
options.B: 30 cm3 is only the leftover excess oxygen. It forgets that the combustion also produces gaseous CO2 and SO2 which must be added to the final total.
options.C: 50 cm3 is correct. Excess O2 = 30 cm3, plus 10 cm3 CO2, plus 10 cm3 SO2 = 50 cm3. Water is liquid at room temperature so is not included.
options.D: 70 cm3 comes from wrongly counting water as a gas: 30 cm3 excess O2 + 10 cm3 CO2 + 10 cm3 SO2 + 20 cm3 H2O = 70 cm3. At room temperature water is liquid, so it contributes no gas volume.
